title: Autonomous Learning From Success and Failure: Goal-Conditioned Supervised Learning with Negative Feedback
abstract: arXiv:2509.03206v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Learning from reward functions and imitation learning of demonstrations are the two principal approaches for training autonomous systems that interact with an environment through action and observation. Both, however, require human specification for each behaviour to be acquired, a problem for long-lived self-adaptive systems whose goals and operating conditions cannot be fully anticipated at design time. Recently, Goal-Conditioned Supervised Learning (GCSL) through self-imitation has been proposed as a self-supervised alternative: by strategically relabelling goals, agents can derive policy insights from their own experiences. Despite its successes, this framework presents two notable limitations: (1) learning exclusively from self-generated experiences can exacerbate the agents' inherent biases; (2) the relabelling strategy allows agents to focus solely on successful outcomes, precluding them from learning from their mistakes

translated_title: 从成功与失败中自主学习：带负反馈的目标条件监督学习
translated_abstract: arXiv:2509.03206v3 公告类型：replace-cross 摘要：基于奖励函数的学习和对示范的模仿学习是训练通过与环境的动作和观察进行交互的自主系统的两种主要方法。然而，这两种方法都需要针对每个待习得的行为进行人工设定，这对于长期运行的自适应系统而言是一个问题，因为此类系统的目标和运行条件在设计时无法被完全预见。最近，通过自我模仿实现的目标条件监督学习被提出作为一种自监督替代方案：通过对目标进行策略性重标注，智能体能够从自身经验中获取策略见解。尽管取得了成功，这一框架仍存在两个显著的局限性：(1) 仅从自我生成的经验中学习可能会加剧智能体固有的偏见；(2) 重标注策略使智能体只能关注成功的结果，从而无法从自身的错误中学习。
tldr: 本文指出目标条件监督学习（GCSL）存在自我经验偏见放大和只能从成功中学习两大局限，并提出引入负反馈机制，使智能体能够同时从成功与失败的经验中自主学习。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies two key limitations of Goal-Conditioned Supervised Learning (GCSL)—amplified bias from self-generated experiences and learning only from successes—and introduces a negative feedback mechanism that enables agents to autonomously learn from both successful and failed experiences.
